NAHHAS:v5p19/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r6.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v5p19/r6.claim: Qatada says the Thamud were destroyed by a blast or cry.
NAHHAS:v5p19/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة بعث الله جل وعز عليهم صيحة فأهدتهم

NAHHAS:v5p19/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r7.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v5p19/r7.claim: One alternative says they were destroyed through their own transgression.
NAHHAS:v5p19/r7.anchor: وقيل فأهلكوا بالطغيان وقيل بالجماعة الطاغية

NAHHAS:v5p19/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r8.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v5p19/r8.claim: Another alternative takes الطاغية to refer to the overwhelming group or event.

NAHHAS:v5p19/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p19/r9.claim: Nahhas prefers Qatada: the verse states the means by which they were destroyed, rather than the reason they were destroyed, as in the account of ʿAd.
NAHHAS:v5p19/r9.anchor: وقول قتادة أصحها أخبر الله بالمعنى الذي أهلكهم به لا بالسبب الذي أهلكهم من أجله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r10.claim: Qatada interprets الطاغية as a cry that exceeded the bounds of every cry.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r10.anchor: و «الطاغية» قال قتادة: معناه الصيحة التي خرجت عن حد كل صيحة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r11.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r11.claim: Some say الطاغية refers to the tyrannical group responsible for destruction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r11.anchor: وقال قوم: المراد بسبب الفئة الطاغية،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r12.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r12.claim: They interpret الطاغية as the tyrannical deed committed by Thamud.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r12.anchor: وقال آخرون منهم مجاهد وابن زيد: المعنى بسبب الفعلة الطاغية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r13.speaker: ابن زيد وأبو عبيدة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r13.claim: They also take الطاغية as a verbal noun for transgression, supported by the reference to Thamud's rebellion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r13.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: ما معناه: «الطاغية» مصدر كالعاقبة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r14.claim: He prefers the cry because it names the means of destruction and parallels ʿAd's wind; other views give Thamud's cause rather than the instrument of destruction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r14.anchor: وأولى الأقوال وأصوبها الأول لأنه مناسب لما ذكر في عاد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r2.claim: Qatada interprets the overwhelming event as the cry that silenced Thamud and the quake that stilled them; Ibn Jarir prefers this.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r2.anchor: بالطاغية} وهي الصيحة التي أسكتتهم، والزلزلة التي أسكنتهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r3.claim: Mujahid interprets the overwhelming event as sins.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r4.speaker: الربيع بن أنس وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r4.claim: Al-Rabi and Ibn Zayd say it means transgression; Ibn Zayd cites Thamud’s denial in their transgression.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r4.anchor: إنها الطغيان، وقرأ ابن زيد: {كذبت ثمود بطغواها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the event with the camel’s killer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r5.anchor: فأهلكوا بالطاغية} قال: يعني: عاقر الناقة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r12.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r12.claim: One view identifies al-taghiyah as the earthquake.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies al-taghiyah as the thunderbolt.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r14.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r14.claim: Qatada says God sent a cry that silenced and killed them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r14.anchor: وعن قتادة : بعث الله عليهم صيحة فأهمدتهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r15.claim: The proposal that al-taghiyah is a verbal noun meaning their transgression is unlikely because it does not pair well with the following fierce wind.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r15.anchor: وقيل : الطاغية مصدر كالعافية ، أي : بطغيانهم ؛ وليس بذاك لعدم الطباق بينها وبين قوله { بريح صرصر

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r14.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r14.claim: Thamud were destroyed by the overpowering cry.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r15.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r15.claim: Thamud were destroyed by a thunderbolt.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r16.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r16.claim: Their sins are given as the cause or means of their destruction.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r17.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r17.claim: Their own transgression is the explanation for their destruction.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r18.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r18.claim: He identifies the طاغية as the woman who hamstrung the she-camel.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r18.anchor: أن الطاغية عاقر الناقة , قاله ابن زيد

ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r7.speaker: أهل اللغة
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r7.claim: Language authorities explain bi-l-ṭāghiya as 'because of their transgression'; the form fāʿila can serve as a verbal noun, like ʿāfiya or ʿāqiba.
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r7.anchor: ومعنى (بالطاغية) عند أهل اللغة بطغيانهم، وفاعلة قد يأتي يمعنى

ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r8.claim: The verse's sense points to their destruction by an overwhelming quake, rather than merely by their own transgression.
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r8.anchor: والذي يدل عليه معنى الآية. - والله أعلم - أنهم أهلكوا بالرجفة الطاغية

ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r9.claim: A very great thing can be called ʿāt or ʿātiya; the description of ʿĀd's fierce wind supports this usage for the overwhelming event.
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r9.anchor: يقال للشيء العظيم عات وعاتية، وكذلك أهلكوا بالطاغية

ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r10.claim: The water that exceeded its proper level is described as transgressing, illustrating how the word conveys excess in magnitude.
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r10.anchor: فوصف الماء بالطغيان لمجاوزته القدر في الكثرة

TABATABAI:69:1-5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:1-5/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:1-5/r7.claim: The nine verses recall several peoples destroyed for denying the Resurrection; this account itself answers what the Great Event is, alongside the later description of the trumpet.
TABATABAI:69:1-5/r7.anchor: هذه الآية وما يتلوها إلى تمام تسع آيات وإن كانت مسوقة للاشارة إلى إجمال قصص قوم نوح وعاد وثمود وفرعون

TABATABAI:69:1-5/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:1-5/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:1-5/r8.claim: The taghiya that destroyed Thamud is variously described in Qur'anic accounts as a shriek, earthquake, or thunderbolt.
TABATABAI:69:1-5/r8.anchor: والمراد بالطاغية الصيحة أو الرجفة أو الصاعقة على اختلاف ظاهر تعبير القرآن في سبب هلاكهم في قصتهم

THALABI:v10p25#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p25#3/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p25#3/r7.claim: Thamud were destroyed by their excessive rebellion and disobedience; the word can also describe their rebellious deed as a quality.
THALABI:v10p25#3/r7.anchor: فأما ثمود فأهلكوا بالطاغية أي بطغيانهم وعصيانهم، وهي مصدر كالحاقة،

THALABI:v10p25#3/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p25#3/r8.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
THALABI:v10p25#3/r8.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd take the word as describing the rebellious deed, supported by the verse saying Thamud denied through their transgression.
THALABI:v10p25#3/r8.anchor: وهذا معنى قول مجاهد وابن زيد، ودليل هذا التأويل قوله سبحانه: كذبت ثمود بطغواها

THALABI:v10p25#3/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p25#3/r9.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p25#3/r9.claim: Qatada says the destructive ṭāghiya was an overwhelming scream that exceeded ordinary cries and killed them.
THALABI:v10p25#3/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة: يعني بالصيحة الطاغية التي جاوزت مقادير الصياح فاهمدتهم

ASAD-NOTES:69:1/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:1/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:1/r2.claim: The translation says Thamud and Ad were overtaken by calamity: Thamud by upheaval, Ad by a storm lasting seven nights and eight days, leaving bodies like hollow palm trunks.
ASAD-NOTES:69:1/r2.anchor: Now as for the Thamud - they were destroyed by a violent upheaval [of the earth]

ELMALILI:69:2-5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:2-5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:2-5/r7.claim: Taghiya means a transgressing event or tyranny; Thamud's was the blast described elsewhere as a cry, a thunderous blast, and the earthquake that accompanied it.
ELMALILI:69:2-5/r7.anchor: “Tâğiye” tuğyan eden, haddini aşan vâkı‘a, tağvâ gibi tuğyan mânasına da gelir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r1.claim: Al-ṭāghiyah means something exceeding its bounds; God turns life-serving forces into destroyers when people exceed limits, as Thamūd did in rebellion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r1.anchor: the Almighty punishes a people according to their attitude.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r2.claim: The Qur’an calls Noah’s floodwater ṭaghā al-māʾ and says Thamūd denied because of rebellion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r2.anchor: the rain water in which the people of Noah (sws) were drowned is called

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r3.claim: Although the sūrah leaves Thamūd’s calamity unnamed, Qur’anic indications discussed in al-Dhāriyāt suggest a thunderbolt from striped winter clouds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r3.anchor: by a thunderbolt which appeared from the striped winter clouds.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r4.claim: An ordinary lightning bolt can become a weapon of destruction by God’s will, and modern scientific advances do not remove humanity’s helplessness before Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r4.anchor: whenever the Almighty wants, He brings to the fore the helplessness of all the scientists of the world.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r4.claim: Most readers use the passive form fa-uhlikū; Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads the verb as active, fa-halakū.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: فأهلكوا: رباعيا مبنيا للمفعول وزيد بن علي: فهلكوا مبنيا للفاعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r5.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r5.claim: Qatāda explains al-ṭāghiyah as a cry beyond the bounds of any ordinary cry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r5.anchor: قال قتادة: بالطاغية: بالصيحة التي خرجت عن حد كل صيحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r6.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r6.claim: Mujāhid and Ibn Zayd say the term means the tyrannical deed they committed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد وابن زيد: بسبب الفعلة الطاغية التي فعلوها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وابن زيد وأبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Zayd, and Abū ʿUbayda parse al-ṭāghiyah as a verbal noun meaning their tyranny.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r8.claim: Other possibilities are the she-camel's killer, with the whole people destroyed for approving it, or a tyrannical faction; al-Ṭabarī prefers the cry because it parallels Aad's destructive wind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r8.anchor: واختار الطبري وغيره أن الطاغية هي الصيحة، وترجيح ذلك مقابلة سبب الهلاك في ثمود بسبب الهلاك في عاد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r8.claim: Thamud were destroyed for their transgression and disbelief; taghiya may be a verbal noun or an adjective for their outrageous act, as in al-Shams.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r8.anchor: {فأما ثمود فأهلكوا بالطاغية} أي بطغيانهم وكفرهم. قيل: هي مصدر، وقيل: نعت أي بفعلهم الطاغية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r9.claim: Qatada says the taghiya was the overpowering cry that exceeded the usual measure of a shout and destroyed them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة: بالصيحة الطاغية، وهي التي جاوزت مقادير الصياح فأهلكتهم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r10.claim: Another report says the cry overflowed its keepers' control, as water overflowed against Noah's people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: طغت على الخزان [فلم يكن لهم عليها سبيل

DURR-FULL:v8p263/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r9.claim: Mujahid says Thamud were destroyed by sins; Ibn Abbas says by the cry.
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {فأهلكوا بالطاغية} قال: بالذنوب وكان ابن عباس يقول: الصيحة

DURR-FULL:v8p263/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r10.claim: A single cry extinguished and destroyed Thamud; the violent wind for ʿAd exceeded its bounds until it pierced their hearts.
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r10.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {فأهلكوا بالطاغية} قال: أرسل الله عليهم صيحة واحدة فأهمدتهم

RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r1.claim: One view takes ṭāghiya as an event exceeding the limit in severity or force, with the root illustrated by 69:11 and 53:17.
RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r1.anchor: أن الطاغية هي الواقعة المجاوزة للحد في الشدة والقوة

RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r2.claim: On that view an omitted noun is understood: some identify the event as an overpowering cry, others as an earthquake or thunderbolt.

RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r3.claim: A second view, transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, takes ṭāghiya as the verbal noun ṭughyān: they were destroyed for rebellion against God, denial of messengers, and unbelief.

RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r4.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj objects that because the next clause names the punishment as a wind, parallelism requires this clause to name a specific punishment too.
RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r4.anchor: قاله الزجاج : أنه لما ذكر في الجملة الثانية

RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r5.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r5.claim: The Qāḍī argues that if ṭāghiya meant the cause of destruction, the wording should say they were destroyed for it, rather than bi-ṭāghiya.
RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r5.anchor: الذي قاله القاضي : وهو أنه لو كان المراد

RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r6.claim: A third view identifies ṭāghiya with the rebellious faction of Thamūd that plotted to hamstring the she-camel; the people were destroyed through that faction’s ill omen.
RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r6.anchor: أي بالفرقة التي طغت من جملة ثمود

RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r7.claim: Alternatively, it means the single man who killed the camel; the whole people were destroyed because they approved his act, and ṭāghiya is an intensive designation.
RAZI-FULL:v30p91#3/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد بالطاغية ذلك الرجل الواحد

STUDYQURAN:69:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:5/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:5/r1.claim: Ṭāghiyah denotes utmost severity and may indicate Thamūd’s calamity: a cry, earthquake, or thunderbolt.
STUDYQURAN:69:5/r1.anchor: Overwhelming translates ṭāghiyah, which implies something that reaches the utmost severity

STUDYQURAN:69:5/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:5/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:69:5/r2.claim: Ṭāghiyah can also mean rebellion or upheaval, from ṭughyān.
STUDYQURAN:69:5/r2.anchor: It could also mean “rebellion” or “upheaval” (ṭughyān; R).

STUDYQURAN:69:5/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:5/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:5/r3.claim: A calamity describes how Thamūd were destroyed, while rebellion describes their sinfulness; the two explanations can both apply.
STUDYQURAN:69:5/r3.anchor: the reference to “rebellion” indicates that they were destroyed by their own sinfulness, though the two are not mutually exclusive

STUDYQURAN:69:5/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:5/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:5/r4.claim: Ṭāghiyah may mean those who overwhelmed or oppressed Thamūd: a powerful minority or individual persuaded them to hamstring God’s she-camel and leave her for dead.
STUDYQURAN:69:5/r4.anchor: “overwhelmed,” by a powerful minority or a single individual who enjoined them to hamstring the she-camel of God (91:13)

TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r1.claim: Al-Tabari identifies Thamud as the people of Salih and says God destroyed them by the overwhelming calamity.
TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره: {فأما ثمود} [الحاقة: 5] قوم صالح، فأهلكهم الله بالطاغية

TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r2.claim: Mujahid interprets the overwhelming calamity as their sins.
TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله عز وجل: {فأهلكوا بالطاغية} [الحاقة: 5] قال: بالذنوب

TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd reads it as their rebellion and disbelief in God's signs, transgressing in disobedience and against God's Book; he cites 91:11.
TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {فأما ثمود فأهلكوا بالطاغية} [الحاقة: 5] فقرأ قول الله: {كذبت ثمود بطغواها} [الشمس: 11]

TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r4.claim: Qatada says God sent a cry that exceeded bounds; in another report it is one cry that silenced them.
TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r4.anchor: عن قتادة {بالطاغية} [الحاقة: 5] قال: أرسل الله عليهم صيحة واحدة فأهمدتهم

TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r5.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that the calamity was an overpowering cry: the verse names what destroyed Thamud, just as the parallel statement names Aad's destroying wind in 69:6.
TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r5.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: معنى ذلك: فأهلكوا بالصيحة الطاغية

TABATABAI:69:6-12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r1.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r1.claim: An alternative takes al-ṭāghiya as a verbal noun like ṭughyān or ṭughwā, meaning the Thamūd were destroyed because of their rebellion; the Sun passage supports this sense.
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r1.anchor: وقيل الطاغية مصدر كالطغيان والطغوى والمعنى فأما ثمود فاهلكوا بسبب طغيانهم

TABATABAI:69:6-12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r2.claim: He prefers the first interpretation because the following verses enumerate modes of destruction; Thamūd’s al-ṭāghiya should therefore denote how they were destroyed.
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r2.anchor: وأول الوجهين أنسب لسياق الآيات التالية حيث سيقت لبيان كيفية إهلاكهم من الإهلاك بالريح أو الأخذ الرابي أو طغيان الماء

BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r5.claim: Thamūd were Arabs whose homes lay at al-Ḥijr between Syria and the Ḥijāz, a place Syrian pilgrims pass on their journeys.
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r5.anchor: وكانوا عربا منازلهم بالحجر بين الشأن والحجاز يراها حجاج الشأن

BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r6.claim: The passive reports that they were destroyed, since the actor, God, is already known and the event is what matters.
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r6.anchor: أي أهلكهم الله لتكذيبهم فأخبر عن الفعل لأنه المراد دون الفاعل

BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r7.claim: Al-Ṭāghiya is an extraordinarily violent blast, exceeding other cries in force and making earth and hearts quake.
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r7.anchor: أي بالصيحة التي جاوزت عن حد سائر الصيحات في الشدة فرجفب منها الأرض

BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r8.claim: The quake and the blast refer to the same Thamūd event, reconciling the account that says the quake seized them with the account that says the cry did.
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r8.anchor: فأخذتهم الرجفة} وبين قوله تعالى : فأخذتهم الصيحة والقصة واحدة

BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r9.claim: Thamūd symbolize people of outward learning veiled from true inward knowledge; because they rejected the inward path and failed to follow a genuine saint, God destroyed them with the fire of distance and veiling, leaving spiritual corruption beneath outward rectitude.
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r9.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أهل العلم الظاهر المحجوبين عن العلوم الحقيقية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r1.speaker: أكثر أهل التفسير والعربية والكلبي ومقاتل وابن عباس ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r1.claim: Most exegetes and grammarians, al-Kalbi, Muqatil, Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid take al-ṭāghiya to mean transgression.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r1.anchor: أكثر أهل التفسير والعربية على أن "الطاغية" هاهنا بمعنى الطغيان. قال الكلبي: الطاغية: طغيانهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r2.claim: Abu ʿUbayda says it means their transgression and disbelief.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r3.claim: The pattern can function as a verbal noun, as in ʿāfiya and ʿāqiba.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r3.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: وفاعله قد يأتي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r4.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r4.claim: Another view, held by Qatada, treats it as an omitted adjective: the overwhelming cry by which they were destroyed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r4.anchor: وهي التي جاوزت مقدار الصياح، وهو قول قتادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r5.claim: Anything ṭāghī is something that exceeds its proper measure.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r5.anchor: والطاغي من كل شيء: ما تجاوز القدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r6.claim: Abu Ishaq prefers the interpretation that Thamud were destroyed by an overwhelming earthquake.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r6.anchor: واختار أبو إسحاق هذا القول، فقال: (الذي يدل عليه معنى الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r7.claim: Because the next verse names the wind that destroyed ʿAd, al-ṭāghiya should likewise name what destroyed Thamud.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p134/r7.anchor: يعني: أنه لما ذكر ما أهلك به عاد، وهو الريح، كذلك "الطاغية" وجب أن تكون اسما

QASHANI:69:5/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:69:5/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:69:5/r3.claim: Both resurrections strike, destroy, and annihilate people through severity; denial of the minor comes from worldly heedlessness, while denial of the major comes from failing to witness it and being veiled from it.
QASHANI:69:5/r3.anchor: وكلتا القيامتين تقرع الناس وتهلكهم وتفنيهم وتستأصلهم بالشدة والقهر

QASHANI:69:5/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:69:5/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:69:5/r4.claim: Thamud may represent people of outward knowledge, called people of little water, who are veiled from true knowledge; deniers may likewise exemplify both the negligent and the excessive.
QASHANI:69:5/r4.anchor: أي: أهل العلم الظاهر المحجوبون عن العلوم الحقيقية

QASHANI:69:5/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:69:5/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:69:5/r5.claim: The overwhelming calamity is an unveiling of the inward and disembodied realm that overcomes and effaces their knowledge; it is the body's destruction.
QASHANI:69:5/r5.anchor: أي: الحالة الكاشفة عن الباطن وعالم التجرد التي تطغى على علومهم فتفنيها

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r2.claim: Thamud denied the afterlife and disobeyed its prophet, so a very severe earthquake destroyed them; “ṭāghiya” describes its overwhelming severity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r2.anchor: şiddetinden dolayı âyette “tâgiye” (azgın) denilen çok ağır bir depremle yok olup gitmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r5.claim: Their fates serve the Muslim community as lessons and as evidence that the power which brought these disasters can also bring about the Resurrection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r5.anchor: bu felâketleri gerçekleştiren gücün kıyameti de gerçekleştireceğine bir kanıt olarak zikredilmiştir

ITQAN:v4p377/r20.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p377/r20.speaker: الكرماني
ITQAN:v4p377/r20.claim: Al-Karmani reports the view that al-Taghiya is the place where Thamud were destroyed.
ITQAN:v4p377/r20.anchor: والطاغية قيل اسم البقعة التي أهلكت بها ثمود حكاهما الكرماني

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p483#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p483#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p483#3/r1.claim: Al-ṭāghiya here means transgression or tyranny.

MAJAZ:v2p267/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p267/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p267/r1.claim: Al-ṭāghiya means their transgression and unbelief.

SAMIN-DURR:69:5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:5/r1.speaker: زيد ابن علي
SAMIN-DURR:69:5/r1.claim: The general reading is passive أهلكوا; Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads active فهلكوا from triliteral هلك.
SAMIN-DURR:69:5/r1.anchor: هذه قراءة العامة. وقرأ زيد ابن علي " فهلكوا " مبنيا للفاعل من هلك ثلاثيا

SAMIN-DURR:69:5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:69:5/r2.claim: الطاغية may mean an overwhelming cry, a transgressive deed, or the tyrannical man who hamstrung the she-camel; on the latter readings it is an intensive adjective.
SAMIN-DURR:69:5/r2.anchor: بالصيحة المتجاوزة للحد. وقيل: بالفعلة الطاغية. وقيل: بالرجل الطاغية

SAMIN-DURR:69:5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:5/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:69:5/r3.claim: The bāʾ is causal in all readings except the cry interpretation, where it marks the instrument, as in عملت بالقدوم.
SAMIN-DURR:69:5/r3.anchor: والباء للسببية على الأقوال كلها، إلا القول الأول فإنها للاستعانة ك " عملت بالقدوم "

SAMIN-DURR:69:5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:5/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:69:5/r4.claim: The verbal noun طغوى used for Thamūd elsewhere supports taking الطاغية as a verbal noun here.

ASAD-NOTES:69:1#n4/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:1#n4/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:1#n4/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to compare the destruction of Thamud with 7:78.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p314/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p314/r4.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p314/r4.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read لا يخفى with yāʾ; the others read لا تخفى with tāʾ, and al-Farisi says both are sound.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p314/r4.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: لا يخفى* [5] بالياء، وقرأ الباقون: لا تخفى بالتاء . كلا الأمرين حسن.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r1.claim: “They were destroyed” means that God destroyed Thamūd.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r1.anchor: ﴿ فأما ثمود فأهلكوا ﴾ أي أهلكهم الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r2.speaker: زيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r2.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads the verb actively: “they perished.”
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r2.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي فهلكوا بالبناء للفاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers al-ṭāghiya as the overwhelming event, namely the shriek; he relates the shriek to 11:67 and the thunderbolt to 41:17.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r3.anchor: الواقعة المجاوزة للحد وهي الصيحة لقوله تعالى في هود وأخذ الذين ظلموا الصيحة وبها فسرت الصاعقة في حم السجدة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r4.claim: The alternative “earthquake” in 7:78 does not conflict: the quake was caused by the shriek, and verses may name a near or more remote cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r4.anchor: أو الرجفة لقوله سبحانه في الأعراف فأخذتهم الرجفة وهي الزلزلة المسببة عن الصيحة فلا تعارض بين الآيات

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r5.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r5.claim: Qatāda glosses al-ṭāghiya as the shriek that exceeded the limit of every other shriek.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r5.anchor: والأول مروي عن قتادة قال أي بالصيحة التي خرجت عن حد كل صيحة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو عبيدة وابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū ʿUbayda, and Ibn Zayd take al-ṭāghiya as a verbal noun meaning transgression, supported by 91:11; Al-Ālūsī prefers the event meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#4/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وأبو عبيدة وابن زيد ما معناه الطاغية مصدر فكأنه قيل بطغيانهم وأيد بقوله تعالى كذبت ثمود بطغواها والمعول عليه الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the paired clauses require parallel causes: saying one people fell through transgression and the other through instrumental wind is unbalanced, since both could be said to fall through transgression. Al-Ālūsī says the issue is parallelism, not event versus substance.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r1.anchor: قول الزمخشري في تضعيف الثاني لعدم الطباق بينها وبين بريح لا أن ذلك لأن أحدهما عين والآخر حدث

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r2.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r2.claim: Mujāhid and Ibn Zayd explain the destruction as punishment for their transgressive deed of hamstringing the she-camel; Al-Ālūsī favors the event reading for the contrast.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r2.anchor: وكذا يرجح الأول على قول مجاهد وابن زيد أيضا أي بسبب الفعلة الطاغية التي فعلوها وهي عقر الناقة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r3.claim: Another view identifies al-ṭāghiya with the camel’s hamstringer; its feminine form is intensive, and all perished because they approved his act.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r3.anchor: وعلى ما قيل الطاغية عاقر الناقة والهاء فيها للمبالغة كما في رجل راوية

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r4.claim: A further view identifies al-ṭāghiya with the transgressive faction; Al-Ālūsī’s preceding parallelism argument explains why he ranks it lower.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r4.anchor: وما قيل أيضا بسبب الفئة الطاغية ووجه الرجحان يعلم مما ذكر

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:5-7/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:5-7/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:5-7/r1.claim: Al-ṭāghiya may be an overwhelmingly severe event, either the blast or the quake, because they denied the Calamity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:5-7/r1.anchor: بالواقعة المجاوزة للحد في الشدة وهي الصيحة، أو الرجفة

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:5-7/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:5-7/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:5-7/r2.claim: Alternatively, it is the verbal noun for their transgression through denial and other acts; this reading as a verbal noun does not agree grammatically with the following account of ʿĀd.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:5-7/r2.anchor: أو بسبب طغيانهم بالتكذيب وغيره على أنها مصدر كالعاقبة وهو لا يطابق قوله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r4.claim: The account first groups both peoples in denial, then distinguishes their punishments because of that denial.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r4.anchor: ولما جمعهم في التكذيب , فصلهم في التعذيب لأجل ذلك التكذيب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r5.claim: Thamūd are the people of the prophet Ṣāliḥ.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r6.claim: The passive wording focuses on the tangible horror of the punishment, rather than on the source from which it came.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r6.anchor: بنى للمجهول قوله : { فأهلكوا } أي بأيسر أمر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r7.claim: Al-ṭāghiyah is a cry exceeding all bounds of severity, making the earth and hearts tremble.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r7.anchor: أي الصيحة التي جاوزت الحد في الشدة فرجفت منها الأرض والقلوب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، مقاتل، أبو عبيدة، ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r1.claim: Al-ṭāghiya means their transgression and disbelief.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r1.anchor: أحدها أنها طغيانهم وكفرهم قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد ومقاتل وأبو عبيدة وابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r2.claim: Al-ṭāghiya can mean transgression; a feminine form may function as a verbal noun, as in ʿāqiba and ʿāfiya.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج ومعنى الطاغية عند أهل اللغة طغيانهم وفاعلة قد يأتي بمعنى المصادر نحو عاقبة وعافية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r3.claim: It means the overpowering cry, which exceeded the ordinary level of a shout and destroyed them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r3.anchor: والثاني بالصيحة الطاغية قاله قتادة وذلك أنها جاوزت مقدار الصياح فأهلكتهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r4.claim: Al-ṭāghiya refers to the person who hamstrung the she-camel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r4.anchor: والثالث أن الطاغية عاقر الناقة قاله ابن زيد

JISHUMI:v10p7056/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r4.claim: Denial is attributed to the people because it is their own act, for which they are punished.
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r4.anchor: ومنها: أن التكذيب فعلهم؛ لذلك أضافه إليهم، وعذبهم عليه.

JISHUMI:v10p7056/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r5.claim: Thamūd were destroyed by the blast and ʿĀd by the wind; the account begins and ends with “day.”
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r5.anchor: ومنها: أن ثمود أهلكت بالصيحة، وعاد بالريح، وابتداؤها كان باليوم، والختم باليوم.

MUQATIL:69:5-12/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r1.claim: Thamud were punished for their transgression, which led them to reject the prophet Salih.
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r1.anchor: يقول: عذبوا بطغيانهم، والطغيان حملهم على تكذيب صالح النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p274/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274/r1.claim: “الطاغية” can mean the event that exceeded the limit in severity.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274/r1.anchor: بالواقعة المجاوزة للحد في الشدة واختلف فيها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p274/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274/r2.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274/r2.claim: One reported view identifies the overwhelming event as an earthquake.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274/r2.anchor: واختلف فيها فقيل الرجفة وقيل الصيحة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p274/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274/r3.claim: Another reported view identifies the overwhelming event as a blast.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274/r3.anchor: فقيل الرجفة وقيل الصيحة وقيل الطاغية مصدر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p274/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274/r4.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274/r4.claim: A further view takes “الطاغية” as a verbal noun meaning their transgression; al-Nasafi says this does not fit what follows.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274/r4.anchor: وقيل الطاغية مصدر كالعافية أي بطغيانهم ولكن هذا لا يطابق قوله

QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r1.claim: The phrase has an elided noun: they were destroyed by the transgressive deed or event.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r2.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r2.claim: Qatada identifies al-taghiyah as the overwhelming shriek, exceeding the limit of cries in its terror, and connects it to the single cry in 54:31.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: أي بالصيحة الطاغية أي المجاوزة للحد أي لحد الصيحات من الهول. كما قال: إنآ أرسلنا عليهم صيحة واحدة

QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r3.claim: Transgression means exceeding the limit; the same root describes the water overflowing in 69:11.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r3.anchor: والطغيان: مجاوزة الحد ومنه: «إنا لما طغا المآء» أي جاوز الحد.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r4.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets al-taghiyah as a thunderbolt.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r5.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r5.claim: Mujahid interprets al-taghiyah as their sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: بالذنوب. وقال الحسن: بالطغيان

QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r6.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r6.claim: Al-Hasan takes al-taghiyah as the verbal noun 'transgression,' like other feminine verbal nouns; the people were destroyed for transgression and disbelief.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن: بالطغيان فهي مصدر كالكاذبة والعاقبة والعافية. أي أهلكوا بطغيانهم وكفرهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies al-taghiyah as the she-camel's killer; all were destroyed because they accepted and supported their leader's act, though only one committed it.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r7.anchor: وقيل: إن الطاغية عاقر الناقة قاله ابن زيد. أي أهلكوا بما أقدم عليه طاغيتهم من عقر الناقة، وكان واحدا

QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r8.claim: A person may be called a taghiyah, like one called a narrator of poetry, a prodigy, a scholar, or a genealogist.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:5/r8.anchor: وقيل له طاغية كما يقال: فلان راوية الشعر، وداهية وعلامة ونسابة.
